entries.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.PotentialParameters.stabilityCounterExample
entries.docstring:
An example of potential parameters that serve as a counterexample to the stability
  condition given in arXiv:hep-ph/0605184.
  This corresponds to the potential:
  `2 * (⟪H.Φ1, H.Φ2⟫_ℂ).im + ‖H.Φ1 - H.Φ2‖ ^ 4`
  which has the property that the quartic term is non-negative and only zero if
  the mass term is also zero, but the potential is not stable.
  In the proof that `stabilityCounterExample_not_potentialIsStable`, we give
  explicit vectors `H.Φ1` and `H.Φ2` that show this potential is not stable.

  This is the first occurrence of such a counterexample in the literature to the best of
  the author's knowledge.
entries.snippet: def stabilityCounterExample : PotentialParameters

entries.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.PotentialParameters.stabilityCounterExample_ξ
entries.snippet:
lemma stabilityCounterExample_ξ :
    stabilityCounterExample.ξ = fun
      | .inl 0 => 0
      | .inr 0 => 0
      | .inr 1 => 1
      | .inr 2 => 0

entries.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.PotentialParameters.stabilityCounterExample_η
entries.snippet:
lemma stabilityCounterExample_η :
    stabilityCounterExample.η = fun μ => fun ν =>
    match μ, ν with
    | .inl 0, .inl 0 => 1
    | .inl 0, .inr 0 => -1
    | .inl 0, .inr 1 => 0
    | .inl 0, .inr 2 => 0
    | .inr 0, .inl 0 => -1
    | .inr 1, .inl 0 => 0
    | .inr 2, .inl 0 => 0
    | .inr 0, .inr 0 => 1
    | .inr 1, .inr 1 => 0
    | .inr 2, .inr 2 => 0
    | .inr 0, .inr 1 => 0
    | .inr 2, .inr 0 => 0
    | .inr 2, .inr 1 => 0
    | .inr 1, .inr 0 => 0
    | .inr 0, .inr 2 => 0
    | .inr 1, .inr 2 => 0

    PotentialIsStable P ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ K : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → ℝ, 0 ≤ K (Sum.inl 0) →
      ∑ μ : Fin 3, K (Sum.inr μ) ^ 2 ≤ K (Sum.inl 0) ^ 2 →
      c ≤ ∑ μ, P.ξ μ * K μ + ∑ a, ∑ b, K a * K b * P.η a b

entries.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.potentialIsStable_iff_forall_euclid
entries.snippet:
lemma potentialIsStable_iff_forall_euclid (P : PotentialParameters) :
    PotentialIsStable P ↔ ∃ c, ∀ K0 : ℝ, ∀ K : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), 0 ≤ K0 →
      ‖K‖ ^ 2 ≤ K0 ^ 2 → c ≤ P.ξ (Sum.inl 0) * K0 + ∑ μ, P.ξ (Sum.inr μ) * K μ
      + K0 ^ 2 * P.η (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inl 0)
      + 2 * K0 * ∑ b, K b * P.η (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inr b) +
      ∑ a, ∑ b, K a * K b * P.η (Sum.inr a) (Sum.inr b)

      ‖K‖ ^ 2 ≤ K0 ^ 2 → c ≤ P.ξ (Sum.inl 0) * K0 + ∑ μ, P.ξ (Sum.inr μ) * K μ
      + K0 ^ 2 * P.η (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inl 0)
      + 2 * K0 * ∑ b, K b * P.η (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inr b) +
      ∑ a, ∑ b, K a * K b * P.η (Sum.inr a) (Sum.inr b)

entries.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.potentialIsStable_of_strong
entries.docstring:
The potential is stable if it is strongly stable, i.e. its quartic term is always positive.
    The proof of this result relies on the compactness of the closed unit ball in
    `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`, and the `extreme value theorem`.
entries.snippet:
lemma potentialIsStable_of_strong (P : PotentialParameters)
    (h : ∀ k, ‖k‖ ^ 2 ≤ 1 → 0 < quarticTermReduced P k) :
    PotentialIsStable P

entries.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.forall_reduced_exists_not_potentialIsStable
entries.docstring:
A lemma invalidating the step in https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0605184 leading to
  equation (4.4).
entries.snippet:
lemma forall_reduced_exists_not_potentialIsStable :
    ∃ P, ¬ PotentialIsStable P ∧ (∀ k : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), ‖k‖ ^ 2 ≤ 1 →
    0 ≤ quarticTermReduced P k ∧ (quarticTermReduced P k = 0 → 0 ≤ massTermReduced P k))

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.lrlOperator_eq
entries.docstring: `𝐀(ε)ᵢ = 𝐱ᵢ𝐩² - (𝐱ⱼ𝐩ⱼ)𝐩ᵢ + ½iℏ(d-1)𝐩ᵢ - mk·𝐫(ε)⁻¹𝐱ᵢ`

    + (2⁻¹ * Complex.I * ℏ * (H.d - 1)) • 𝐩[i] - (H.m * H.k) • 𝐫[ε,-1] ∘L 𝐱[i]

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.lrlOperatorSqr_eq
entries.docstring:
The square of the (regularized) LRL vector operator is related to the (regularized) Hamiltonian
  `𝐇(ε)` of the hydrogen atom, square of the angular momentum `𝐋²` and powers of `𝐫(ε)` as
  `𝐀(ε)² = 2m 𝐇(ε)(𝐋² + ¼ℏ²(d-1)²) + m²k² - m²k²ε²𝐫(ε)⁻² + mkε²𝐫(ε)⁻³(𝐋² + ¼ℏ²(d-1)(d-3))`.
entries.snippet:
lemma lrlOperatorSqr_eq (hε : 0 < ε) : H.lrlOperatorSqr ε =
    (2 * H.m) • (H.hamiltonianReg ε) ∘L
      (𝐋² + (4⁻¹ * ℏ ^ 2 * (H.d - 1) ^ 2 : ℝ) • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space H.d, ℂ))
    + (H.m * H.k) ^ 2 • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space H.d, ℂ)
    - ((H.m * H.k) ^ 2 * ε ^ 2) • 𝐫[ε,-2]
    + (H.m * H.k * ε ^ 2) • 𝐫[ε,-3] ∘L
      (𝐋² + (4⁻¹ * ℏ^2 * (H.d - 1) * (H.d - 3) : ℝ) •
      ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space H.d, ℂ))

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator
entries.docstring:
Component `i j` of the angular momentum operator is the continuous linear map
from `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` to itself defined by `𝐋ᵢⱼ ≔ 𝐱ᵢ∘𝐩ⱼ - 𝐱ⱼ∘𝐩ᵢ`.
entries.snippet: def angularMomentumOperator {d : ℕ} (i j : Fin d) : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator_apply_fun
entries.snippet:
lemma angularMomentumOperator_apply_fun {d : ℕ} (i j : Fin d) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    𝐋[i,j] ψ = 𝐱[i] (𝐩[j] ψ) - 𝐱[j] (𝐩[i] ψ)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma angularMomentumOperator_apply {d : ℕ} (i j : Fin d) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) (x : Space d) :
    𝐋[i,j] ψ x = 𝐱[i] (𝐩[j] ψ) x - 𝐱[j] (𝐩[i] ψ) x

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperatorSqr
entries.docstring: The square of the angular momentum operator, `𝐋² ≔ ½ ∑ᵢⱼ 𝐋ᵢⱼ∘𝐋ᵢⱼ`.
entries.snippet: def angularMomentumOperatorSqr {d : ℕ} : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperatorSqr_apply_fun
entries.snippet:
lemma angularMomentumOperatorSqr_apply_fun {d : ℕ} (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    𝐋² ψ = (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • ∑ i, ∑ j, 𝐋[i,j] (𝐋[i,j] ψ)

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperatorSqr_apply
entries.snippet:
lemma angularMomentumOperatorSqr_apply {d : ℕ} (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) (x : Space d) :
    𝐋² ψ x = (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, ∑ j, 𝐋[i,j] (𝐋[i,j] ψ) x

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.position_commutation_momentum
entries.docstring: The canonical commutation relations: `[xᵢ, pⱼ] = iℏ δᵢⱼ𝟙`.

lemma position_commutation_momentum {d : ℕ} (i j : Fin d) : ⁅𝐱[i], 𝐩[j]⁆ =

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumOperator

entries.snippet:
lemma momentumOperator_apply_fun {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :

entries.name: QuantumMechanics.UnboundedOperator
entries.docstring:
An `UnboundedOperator` is a linear map from a submodule of the Hilbert space
  to the Hilbert space, assumed to be both densely defined and closable.

@[ext]
structure UnboundedOperator
    (HS : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup HS] [InnerProductSpace ℂ HS] [CompleteSpace HS]
    extends LinearPMap ℂ HS HS where
  dense_domain : Dense (domain : Set HS)
  is_closable : toLinearPMap.IsClosable

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.ComponentIdx.complexify_comp_dropPairEmb
entries.docstring:
`complexify` commutes with precomposition by `dropPairEmb`.
  We use `fun k => b (Pure.dropPairEmb i j k)` and direct application
  `(ComponentIdx.complexify b) (Pure.dropPairEmb i j m)` rather than composition so that
  dependent `ComponentIdx` types unify correctly (avoiding `Function.comp` type mismatch).
entries.snippet:
@[simp]
lemma ComponentIdx.complexify_comp_dropPairEmb
    {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → realLorentzTensor.Color}
    {i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)} (b : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor) c) (m : Fin n) :
    (ComponentIdx.complexify (c := c ∘ Pure.dropPairEmb i j)
      (fun k => b (Pure.dropPairEmb i j k))) m =
    (ComponentIdx.complexify (c := c) b) (Pure.dropPairEmb i j m)

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.toComplex_contrP_basisVector
entries.docstring:
For a real basis vector, `toComplex(contrP(basisVector c b))` equals
  `contrP(basisVector (colorToComplex ∘ c) (complexify b))` (complex species).
entries.snippet:
lemma toComplex_contrP_basisVector {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1 + 1) → realLorentzTensor.Color}
    {i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)} (h : i ≠ j ∧ (realLorentzTensor).τ (c i) = c j)
    (b : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor) c) :
    toComplex (c := c ∘ Pure.dropPairEmb i j)
      (Pure.contrP (S := realLorentzTensor) i j h (Pure.basisVector c b))
      =
    Pure.contrP (S := complexLorentzTensor) i j
      (by
        simpa [Function.comp_apply] using And.intro h.1
          (by simpa [tau_colorToComplex] using congrArg colorToComplex h.2))
      (Pure.basisVector (colorToComplex ∘ c) (ComponentIdx.complexify b))

entries.name: realLorentzTensor.toComplex_evalP_basisVector
entries.docstring:
For a real basis vector, `toComplex(evalP(basisVector c b))` equals
  `evalP(basisVector (colorToComplex ∘ c) (complexify b))` (complex species).
entries.snippet:
lemma toComplex_evalP_basisVector {n : ℕ} {c : Fin (n + 1) → realLorentzTensor.Color}
    (i : Fin (n + 1)) (b : Fin ((realLorentzTensor).repDim (c i)))
    (b' : ComponentIdx (S := realLorentzTensor) c) :
    toComplex (c := c ∘ i.succAbove)
      (Pure.evalP (S := realLorentzTensor) i b (Pure.basisVector c b'))
      =
    permT (S := complexLorentzTensor) (σ := (id : Fin n → Fin n))
      (by simp [Function.comp_apply])
      (Pure.evalP (S := complexLorentzTensor) i (evalIdxToComplex (c := c) i b)
        (Pure.basisVector (colorToComplex ∘ c) (ComponentIdx.complexify b')))
